newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing. [CORRECTED 13:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing. [CORRECTED 13:20 GMT]

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokesman Jochem Kubosch said the EU and Japan had agreed on a quota of 1,092,000 Japanese cars that can be imported in the EU's market in 1997. He said Japan sold 808,000 cars in the EU last year although the quota was for 1,093,000 (corrects from 1,003,000) vehicles.

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the Commission decided on Tuesday to challenge the Council decision to shut out the European Parliament on legislation on beef labelling. He said the Commission was ready to go to the European Court of Justice and would discuss with the parliament whether to join forces against the Council on this.
The Commission has two months from the date of publication of the Council decision to take legal action, Vale de Almeida said. He said the legal action would not suspend the contested decision.
Spokesman Willy Helin said the Commission had decided to postpone by another two weeks a decision to ban French measures to protect jobs in its textile industry.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/248: Commission pledges continuing support for international fund for Ireland
- IP/97/249: Commission proposes to enhance EU support to heavily indebted poor ACP states
- IP/97/251: Commission gives green light to Maribel scheme in support of manual labour
- IP/97/252: Commission approves Dutch measure to lower the cost of research personnel
- IP/97/254: G7 Global Marketplace for SMEs Conference, 7-9 April, Bonn
- IP/97/255: Operation ECHO-FLIGHT extended in East and Central Africa
- Eurostat news release: Accounting rules - complementary decisions of Eurostat on deficit and debt
